description: Imbuia is a medium-density Brazilian hardwood with olive to dark brown, often figured heartwood and a spicy scent when worked. It is prized for fine furniture, cabinetry, veneer, and turned objects.

hazards.summary: Occupational asthma caused by imbuia dust was described in a South African worker. A NIOSH-funded review lists imbuia among woods with a positive specific challenge test.
All wood dust, including imbuia, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed imbuia (Ocotea porosa) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Olive-brown to deep chocolate-brown heartwood with variegated darker and golden streaks, no sapwood visible. Fine to medium texture with straight to wavy grain and patches of curly figure that shimmer slightly, moderate natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.

notes_internal: Jeebhay-1996 has no abstract; level 1 rests on SENSOR-2017 Table 3 (states listed species had positive specific antigen challenge) plus an occupationalasthma.com index entry (lead only) noting an immediate challenge reaction. Confirm from full text. Schlunssen-2018 also cites Pitt ML et al. S Afr Med J 1985;67:82 (not found on PubMed, not cited). Schlunssen uses Phoebe porosa; current name Ocotea porosa per GBIF (POWO/WFO not reachable). No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
